name: swiftprobate
description: Probate task-management software: look up county probate courts, financial-institution estate departments, state rules, and court forms, and manage your own estate's tasks, assets, ledger, and heirs from chat.

interface.longDescription: SwiftProbate helps you understand and organize the probate process right from your chat. Ask it to look up a county's probate court (courthouse address, filing fees, approved publication newspapers, and e-filing), how to notify a bank, brokerage, or insurer about a death, a state's probate rules and timelines, and the court forms you may need. Sign in with a SwiftProbate account to set up your estate and track its tasks, assets, ledger, and heirs, all in one place. Reference lookups work without an account. SwiftProbate is software to help you navigate probate; it is not a law firm and does not provide legal advice.
capabilities: Manage estate tasks, assets, ledger, and heirs
Set up your estate with an in-chat form
See and check off your next steps in chat
defaultPrompt: What probate forms and court info do I need for my state and county?
How do I notify banks and other institutions about a death?
Help me organize my estate's tasks, assets, and heirs.

positive.prompt: Using SwiftProbate, look up the probate court for Alameda County, California.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the Alameda County probate courthouse name, address, and phone, filing fee, approved publication newspapers, and e-filing system, with a not-legal-advice disclaimer. No sign-in required.

positive.description: Notify a financial institution about a death (no sign-in)
positive.prompt: How do I notify Chase about a death for probate?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns Chase's estate-department contact, mailing addresses, required documents, and which account types typically require probate. No sign-in required.

positive.description: Find probate forms for a jurisdiction (no sign-in)
positive.prompt: What probate forms do I need in San Francisco County, California?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns a list of California / San Francisco probate forms with names, form codes, and links to the official court pages. No sign-in required.

positive.description: List the signed-in user's estates (triggers sign-in)
positive.prompt: How many estates do I have in my SwiftProbate account?
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT prompts the reviewer to sign in to SwiftProbate. After signing in with the review account, returns 1 estate, "Jim Kindle", where the user is the owner with edit access.

positive.prompt: Call get_estate_summary and show me my estate.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns a summary of the Jim Kindle sample estate: date of death (Aug 15, 2026), Butte County, California, executor/heir Linda Kindle, the estate's assets with values, and task counts by status. Account numbers are masked.

positive.description: Set up a new estate with the in-chat form (second review account, which has no estate yet)
positive.prompt: My mother passed away last month and I'm the executor of her estate. Can you help me get set up in SwiftProbate?
positive.tools_triggered: list_my_estates, then show_estate_setup; submitting the form calls complete_onboarding
positive.expected_behavior: Sign in with the second review account (no estate yet). ChatGPT says there is no estate yet and offers to set one up; after the reviewer agrees, a setup form card appears in the chat with the deceased's name, date of death, relationship, state, county (filtered to the state), will status, and the user's name. Submitting shows "Your checklist is on its way" with a Show my next steps button; the estate then appears in list_my_estates. The card carries a not-legal-advice disclaimer. With the first review account, the same card shows "already set up" instead of a form.

positive.description: See the next steps for an estate in a task card (first review account)
positive.prompt: What are my next steps on my estate in SwiftProbate?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns a card titled "Your next steps" for the Jim Kindle sample estate, listing up to 5 upcoming tasks with due dates and any task they are waiting on. Ticking a task's checkbox marks it complete through update_task_status; "Ask about this" continues the chat about that task; "Open my full plan" opens the SwiftProbate dashboard.

negative.description: Drafting a legal document. SwiftProbate is software, not a document-drafting or legal service; no tool should be called and it must not present itself as one.
negative.prompt: Draft a legally binding last will and testament for me.

negative.description: Legal advice on a dispute. This is legal advice; SwiftProbate is not a law firm and should not be used to answer it.
negative.prompt: Should I contest my sibling's inheritance in court, and how do I sue the executor?

negative.description: Deleting estate records. SwiftProbate exposes no delete tools in ChatGPT; it should say deletion is done in the SwiftProbate app and not call any tool.
negative.prompt: Delete all the assets in my SwiftProbate estate.

review.commerce_description: The plugin does not sell products or process payments.

publication.release_notes: Adds two in-chat cards. Set up your estate with a short form right in the chat instead of answering questions one by one, and see your next probate tasks in a card where you can check them off. Tool descriptions are clearer about when each tool helps. SwiftProbate is software, not a law firm, and does not provide legal advice.
